findings.title: GET /cards/physical/{card_id} lists 201 but no 404 or other errors
findings.evidence: Responses only define "201" (success) and "400" ("raises CardInvalidInput"). The success code is 201 rather than 200, and no 401/403/404 is documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success code to 200 and document 401, 403, and 404 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse.

findings.title: Many operations document no error responses at all
findings.location: PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}; DELETE /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}/suspension; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual/{card_id}; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements/{reimbursement_id}; PATCH /developer/v1/transactions/{transaction_id}; GET /developer/v1/cards/vault/{card_id}
findings.evidence: These operations define only success responses (e.g. PATCH card: "200" only; GET virtual card: "200" only; GET reimbursement: "200" only), while sibling operations such as GET /cards/physical/{card_id} document "400" with DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same 400/401/404 error responses with DeveloperApiErrorResponse to every operation that accepts IDs or bodies.

findings.title: Error responses on POST /cards/physical use untyped string schema
findings.evidence: "400":{"description":"Error","content":{"application/json":{"schema":{"type":"string"}}}}
findings.suggested_fix: Use $ref DeveloperApiErrorResponse, as the other 400 responses do, so the client gets a typed error object.

findings.title: Error responses declared inconsistently across the API
findings.evidence: POST /reimbursements/mileage has only "200" and "401" (no 400 for invalid body). POST /reimbursement/submit-receipt documents 400/401/404 but no error case for the 201 path. POST /cards/vault only documents "400" with no 401 even though it requires security.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the same set of error codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 429 if used) on each write endpoint, and state which errors each one can return.

findings.title: Missing security on mileage creation endpoint
findings.evidence: "security":[]} while the operation returns "401" Unauthorized. Every other write operation declares oauth2 scopes (e.g. POST /reimbursement/submit-receipt uses "reimbursements:write").
findings.suggested_fix: Add security: [{oauth2: ["reimbursements:write"]}] and remove the empty override.

findings.title: Path naming inconsistent: reimbursement vs reimbursements
findings.evidence: Path "/developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt" uses singular "reimbursement", while all other reimbursement paths use "/developer/v1/reimbursements" and "/developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/submit-receipt, keeping the old path documented as deprecated if needed.

findings.title: Inconsistent query param casing and paths for virtual cards
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual (query params userId, entity_id, is_terminated); GET /developer/v1/transactions (orderByAmountAsc, order_by_amount_desc)
findings.evidence: Query "userId" is camelCase while "user_id" is used elsewhere; "orderByAmountAsc" is camelCase while the sibling "order_by_amount_desc" is snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Use snake_case consistently: user_id and order_by_amount_asc. Keep the old names as deprecated aliases if they must stay.

findings.title: Pagination parameters differ between list endpoints
findings.evidence: Only the virtual-cards list defines "start" and "page_size" with a default of 20 and "page_size" is absent from physical cards. Physical cards returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with no start/page_size parameters at all. Transactions alone has include_count, which can return total_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Give all list endpoints the same pagination parameters (start, page_size with bounds) and document why total_count exists only on transactions.

findings.title: page_size bounds are not enforced in the schema
findings.evidence: Description says "The value must be between 2 and 100", but the schema is only {"default":20,"type":"integer"} with no minimum or maximum.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "minimum": 2 and "maximum": 100 to the schema so generated clients validate the range.

findings.title: Physical cards list uses non-standard response for 400 description
findings.evidence: Description of 400 is "raises CardInvalidInput" — an internal exception name rather than a documented error condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual invalid input conditions in plain language, e.g. which filter combinations are rejected.

findings.title: Nullable fields in Reimbursement list lack documented meaning
findings.evidence: Schema lists "employee_id" as "nullable":true with no description of when it is null; "distance" is nullable with the description 'for mileage reimbursements' but no statement that it is null for other types; "payee_amount" is nullable.
findings.suggested_fix: State the conditions under which each nullable field is null, and mark it as required or optional consistently.

findings.title: Deprecated amount field still typed as number, sibling typed as string
findings.evidence: In Transaction, "amount" is {"deprecated":true,"type":"number"}, but in SingleTransaction the same field is {"deprecated":true,"type":"string"}.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for the same field in both schemas, and align the deprecated field's documentation.

findings.title: Transaction.required omits many fields that are nullable or present
findings.evidence: Both schemas list "card_holder" absent from required, though card_holder is documented; "merchant_category_code" and "fund_id" are missing from required in both schemas while also readOnly. Fields like "amount" are not required but "entity_amount" is required and nullable.
findings.suggested_fix: Review the required arrays so non-null guarantees match the actual API behavior, and document the nullable-but-required pairs.

findings.title: Reimbursement required array includes nullable fields with no nullability note
findings.evidence: Required list includes "accounting_date", "approved_at", "distance", "employee_id" and others that are declared "nullable":true, while "created_at" and "id" are required and non-nullable.
findings.suggested_fix: Document clearly that these fields are always present but may be null, so generated types use optional-and-nullable rather than surprise nulls.

findings.title: Card vault endpoint returns PAN/CVV with no declared protection
findings.evidence: CardDetails.properties.pan 'Primary account number(PAN) of the card.' and cvv 'Card verfication value.' are plain strings; operation has only security oauth2 cards:read_vault and no x-headers, step-up, or response-caching constraints declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare Cache-Control: no-store on responses, mark pan/cvv as writeOnly/sensitive, and document an extra authorization requirement or restricted scope.

findings.title: Full card number exposed in physical card shipping schema
findings.evidence: "full_card_number":{"type":"string","description":"The full card number."} is returned under CardShipping, which is embedded in GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} responses under cards:read scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove full_card_number from the general PhysicalCard read model or gate it behind cards:read_vault with no-store caching.

findings.title: PAN and CVV in PCICardDetails lack format or constraints
findings.evidence: pan {"type":"string"} and cvv {"type":"string"} have no pattern, minLength, maxLength, or writeOnly marker, while 'expiration' is described only as 'MMYY' text with no pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Add pattern/length constraints (e.g., cvv ^[0-9]{3,4}$, expiration ^(0[1-9]|1[0-2])[0-9]{2}$) and mark sensitive fields clearly.

findings.title: POST /cards/physical and mileage POST lack declared security
findings.evidence: "security":[]` on the mileage create operation, while all other operations declare oauth2 scopes; responses list only a 401.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the oauth2 scope (e.g., reimbursements:write) for this operation or document why it is public.

findings.title: Pagination parameter naming inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is 'userId' while physical cards and reimbursements use 'user_id'; transactions use 'order_by_date_asc' but virtual cards and transactions use 'orderByAmountAsc' vs 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize all query parameters on snake_case (userId→user_id, orderByAmountAsc→order_by_amount_asc).

findings.title: Same concept named differently: limit vs spend_limit vs fund
findings.evidence: The fund concept appears as limit_id, spend_limit_id, spend_allocation_id, and fund_id across endpoints, with 'limit_id' described as 'Alias of fund'.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one canonical name (fund_id) and mark the others deprecated consistently across all endpoints.

findings.title: Inconsistent pagination parameter and response shapes
findings.evidence: Virtual card list has 'start' and 'page_size' with default 20 but no maximum; transactions responses include total_count/total_count_capped via DeveloperAPICountedPage, while the virtual cards response uses DeveloperAPINestedPage with no count; 'page_size' is described as 'between 2 and 100' but has no minimum/maximum in schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Encode page_size minimum 2 and maximum 100 in schema for all list endpoints and use one page object across them.

findings.title: Physical card list 'id' fields lack pagination; start cursor undocumented
findings.evidence: Physical card list has no 'start' or 'page_size' parameters, yet returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a page.next link.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters matching the other list endpoints, or remove the pagination envelope.

findings.title: Amount fields use mixed types and units
findings.location: Transaction.amount; ApiSignedAmount.value; CurrencyAmount.amount; ApiReimbursementAmount.value; GET /developer/v1/transactions min_amount/max_amount
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is {"type":"number"} (deprecated) while entity_amount.value is an integer minor unit; SingleTransaction.amount is {"type":"string"}; min_amount is oneOf decimal string or number with no unit stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Use integer minor units everywhere, remove the conflicting amount type, and state the unit in min_amount/max_amount descriptions.

findings.title: Date filter formats are inconsistent
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements (from_transaction_date, from_date, from_submitted_at); PATCH transaction, reimbursement.transaction_date
findings.evidence: Reimbursement list filters use format date-time, Reimbursement.transaction_date uses format date, and 'to_transaction_date' has description 'Data.' with no meaningful text.
findings.suggested_fix: Use consistent date/date-time formats per concept and replace placeholder descriptions like 'Data.' with real descriptions.

findings.title: Placeholder and missing descriptions on parameters
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date has description "Data."; include_merchant_data has description "Data." on the single-transaction endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace placeholder descriptions with accurate text describing the filter's semantics.

findings.title: Operation summaries contradict their actions
findings.evidence: GET virtual card has summary "Permanently delete this resource" while it is a read operation; DELETE physical card says 'Terminate a card'.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the GET summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and align terminology for physical card deletion.

findings.title: Inconsistent 2xx codes and error documentation across operations
findings.evidence: GET single physical card returns 201 instead of 200; POST /cards/physical 400 error uses schema type string while other 400s use DeveloperApiErrorResponse; PATCH has no 400/401/404 responses.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for GET, use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all error responses, and document 401/404 consistently.

findings.title: Idempotency key defined inconsistently
findings.evidence: Vault creation takes optional header X-Idempotency-Key, while receipt upload requires body field idempotency_key; POST /cards/physical and POST /reimbursements/mileage have no idempotency mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header) across all POST endpoints and make it required for money-moving or card-creating operations.

findings.title: Transaction amount fields lack unit and sign clarity
findings.evidence: "amount":{"deprecated":true,"description":"Deprecated. Use `entity_amount`.","type":"number"} while SingleTransaction.amount is typed "type":"string". Same field, different types across schemas.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for `amount` in both schemas, state its unit (major units or minor units), or remove it given the deprecation.

findings.title: Minor-unit amounts in split endpoint lack currency context
findings.evidence: "amount":{"description":"Amount in minor units (e.g. 5000 = $50.00).","type":"integer"} with no currency field or range, while ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody has no currency_code and the split must sum to the transaction amount in an unspecified currency.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the currency the split amounts are denominated in, whether it is the entity settlement currency, and whether negative values are allowed for refunds.

findings.title: Spend limit amount has no unit or currency requirement
findings.evidence: "amount":{"description":"the amount of money represented in the smallest denomination...","type":"integer"} with no minimum; "currency_code":{"default":"USD"}. No minimum or maximum, and the request schema lacks a `minimum` even though limits must be positive.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum (for example 1 or 0), maximum, and an explicit currency enum or supported-currency list for limit requests.

findings.title: Allowed overage percent has inconsistent type declarations
findings.evidence: Request: "maximum":100,"minimum":0,"oneOf":[{"format":"decimal","type":"string"},{"type":"number"}]; response: "format":"decimal","type":"string". Request accepts string or number; response only returns string; the `maximum`/`minimum` are placed outside oneOf.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one wire type (string decimal preferred for money-like values), state the precision, and apply the bounds consistently to both request and response.

findings.title: Timestamp formats are inconsistent and malformed in examples
findings.evidence: Example values such as "created_at":"2023-08-20T:00:00+00:00" and "submitted_at":"2023-08-20T:00:00+00:00" are not valid ISO8601 date-times; Transaction.accounting_date is format date-time but PhysicalCard.created_at is format date-time with example "2022-05-04T00:00:00+00:00".
findings.suggested_fix: Correct examples to full ISO8601 timestamps (for example 2023-08-20T00:00:00Z) and state the timezone rule.

findings.title: Transaction state enum mixes filter sentinel with real states
findings.evidence: Query enum: ["ALL","CLEARED","COMPLETION","DECLINED","ERROR","PENDING","PENDING_INITIATION"]; response state enum includes "ALL" too. A response record can never legitimately be ALL.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate the filter enum from the response enum and remove ALL from the response state enum.

findings.title: Date and datetime filters have no timezone or range rules
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements (from_transaction_date, to_transaction_date, from_date, to_date) and GET /developer/v1/transactions (from_date, to_date)
findings.evidence: "to_transaction_date" description is just "Data."; from_date is "format":"date-time" with no timezone or inclusive/exclusive statement, while from_transaction_date says "after this date" and from_date (transactions) says "after" vs "after this date" elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe each boundary as inclusive or exclusive, require a timezone offset, and replace the placeholder 'Data.' description.

findings.title: Pagination page_size range is not enforced in schema
findings.evidence: Description: "The value must be between 2 and 100." but schema is only {"default":20,"type":"integer"} with no minimum or maximum.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "minimum":2 and "maximum":100 to the schema so clients and generators can validate it.

findings.title: Pagination cursor 'start' is an untyped opaque string with no contract
findings.evidence: "description":"The ID of the last entity of the previous page...","schema":{"type":"string"}. The physical cards list has no pagination params at all, and the `next` links use placeholder "<resources>?<new_params>".
findings.suggested_fix: Document start as an opaque cursor, prefer using the next URL, and add pagination parameters to the physical cards list or explain why it is unpaginated.

findings.title: Physical card list has no pagination controls
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with page.next, but parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only; no start or page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters matching the other list endpoints, or document the maximum result size.

findings.title: Enum of reimbursement state is huge and can change without versioning
findings.evidence: Enum includes 25 values such as "EXPORT_MARKED_AS_FAILED", "REIMBURSED_VIA_PUSH" and "PUSH_PAYMENT_INITIATED", with no statement on whether new values may be added.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that enums are open and clients must handle unknown values, and publish a deprecation policy.

findings.title: Virtual card list filter uses inconsistent parameter naming
findings.evidence: Virtual cards: "name":"userId" while every other filter is snake_case (user_id, entity_id). Transactions: "name":"orderByAmountAsc" alongside order_by_amount_desc.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to user_id and order_by_amount_asc, keeping the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Reimbursement user_id query parameter is undocumented and duplicated
findings.evidence: The user_id parameter has no description, unlike all other parameters on the same operation, and there is no description of how it interacts with reimbursee-related filters.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description stating what user_id filters (reimbursee or submitter).

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload has undefined file constraints
findings.evidence: "receipt":{... "UploadedFileRequestBody" format binary} with no maxLength, allowed MIME types, or size limit. The description only says 'Receipt image or PDF'.
findings.suggested_fix: Document accepted MIME types, maximum file size, and the expected behavior on oversize files.

findings.title: Idempotency key is inconsistent across endpoints
findings.evidence: Vault: header "X-Idempotency-Key" with minLength 1 and maxLength 255. Receipt upload: body field "idempotency_key" with no length limits and no statement of retention window or whether it is required (it is listed in required).
findings.suggested_fix: Use one mechanism (header with the same length bounds) across all POST endpoints and document the retention window and duplicate-key response.

findings.title: Reimbursement state values lack clear approval-state meanings
findings.evidence: State enum includes APPROVED, PENDING, INIT, DRAFT, REJECTED, PROCESSING, EXPORTED, REIMBURSED, REIMBURSED_VIA_PUSH, MANUALLY_REIMBURSED, etc. Descriptions are terse, e.g. "INIT":"Init", "PENDING":"Pending Review", "PUSH_PAYMENT_FAILED":"Payment failed", "EXPORT_FAILED":"Payment failed".
findings.suggested_fix: Define each state's meaning, which states mean money has moved, and which are terminal, and make the two 'Payment failed' labels distinct.

findings.title: Transaction state and approval_status lack defined meanings
findings.evidence: approval_status enum: AWAITING_EMPLOYEE, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_CHANGES_REQUESTED, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_MISSING_ITEMS, AWAITING_REVIEWER, FULLY_APPROVED, but no x-enum-descriptions are given. The state enum has descriptions but 'COMPLETION' and 'ERROR' are vague.
findings.suggested_fix: Add x-enum-descriptions for approval_status and state the required action and who acts for each value.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'approved' filter and approved_at are unclear
findings.evidence: "Filter for reimbursements that are approved or not approved. If not specified, returns all reimbursements." and approved_at: "Time at which the reimbursement is approved." No field says who approved it.
findings.suggested_fix: State which approver is recorded and whether approved_at changes if a reimbursement is re-approved.

findings.title: No approver identity or approval history in any response
findings.evidence: Reimbursement has created_at, submitted_at, approved_at, updated_at, but no approved_by, rejected_by, or history field. Transaction has updated_at only, described as 'Approximate transaction updated timestamp'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add fields or an audit endpoint identifying who approved, rejected, or changed each item and when.

findings.title: updated_at is described as approximate and computed
findings.evidence: "Approximate transaction updated timestamp used by the `updated_after` filter. Computed as the latest of user transaction time, settlement time, and transaction interaction state update time."
findings.suggested_fix: Explain what changes count as an update and whether a memo or category change moves this timestamp, so audit windows are reliable.

findings.title: Amount fields use different units and types
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is a deprecated 'number' (e.g. 90.0, dollars) while entity_amount.value is an integer in cents (9000). SingleTransaction.amount is typed 'string'. Transaction.entity_amount is signed; ApiReimbursementAmount.value is 'non-negative'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type and unit for all amounts and document the unit in each description, including whether the value is dollars or cents.

findings.title: Amount sign convention is inconsistent across schemas
findings.evidence: ApiSignedAmount: "May be negative for refunds or credits." ApiReimbursementAmount: "The non-negative amount" with minimum 0. Reimbursement paybacks (PAYBACK_FULL, PAYBACK_PARTIAL) have no stated sign.
findings.suggested_fix: State whether reimbursement payback amounts are positive or negative and which direction money flows.

findings.title: Date fields lack timezone and meaning clarity
findings.evidence: transaction_date is type 'date' while created_at is 'date-time'. Filter descriptions: from_transaction_date 'Filter by underlying transaction date (after this date).' and to_transaction_date 'Data.' ; from_date 'created after this date' vs Transaction from_date 'user_transaction_time'.
findings.suggested_fix: Make to_transaction_date's description meaningful, state inclusive/exclusive bounds, and name the exact timestamp each date filter uses.

findings.title: Transaction filter from_date uses a different date than list labels imply
findings.evidence: "Filter for transactions with a `user_transaction_time` after the given date" while order_by_date_asc says "Sort transactions by `user_transaction_date`" (a different field name).
findings.suggested_fix: Use one consistent date field name and state whether from_date and order_by_date refer to the same timestamp.

findings.title: Accounting date meaning depends on undisclosed settings
findings.evidence: "Based on the cleared date, transaction date, or a manually overridden date, depending on your accounting preferences in Ramp." and reimbursement: "uses the transaction date or reviewed date according to accounting sync settings".
findings.suggested_fix: Add a field showing which source produced the value (cleared, transaction, reviewed, or override) so the compliance reviewer can see it.

findings.title: Split line item rules conflict or are undocumented
findings.evidence: Description: "Send line_items with amounts (in minor units)" but ApiTransactionLineItem.amount is a CurrencyAmount object. Field selection says 'Provide exactly one of field_id or field_external_id' but neither is required in the schema. Operation is marked "x-destructive":true with no description of what is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: State the request amount format, enforce the 'exactly one' rules in the schema, and describe what existing memos or coding are overwritten.

findings.title: Mileage create endpoint has no auth and an unclear default
findings.evidence: "security":[] and the only response listed is 401 'Unauthorized'. Request field distance_units has no default or description and spend_allocation_id is described as 'the fund'.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the required OAuth scope, and document the default distance unit and whether the fund is the same as the spend limit.

findings.title: Receipt upload retry behaviour and idempotency key duplicated
findings.evidence: Receipt upload takes idempotency_key in the form body and it is required, while the vault create uses header X-Idempotency-Key which is optional. Receipt schema description says only "Caller-supplied key that makes upload retries idempotent."
findings.suggested_fix: Use one mechanism for idempotency and state what happens when a key is reused with different content.

findings.title: Physical card 'state' and 'is_suspended' overlap without explanation
findings.evidence: state enum includes SUSPENDED, and is_suspended: 'Whether the card is suspended.' Suspend endpoint says "The suspension is revertable." but terminate says "irreversible" without saying who can reverse it.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain how the two fields relate and record who suspended the card and when.

findings.title: Transaction split PATCH is destructive yet mislabeled and undocumented for auth
findings.evidence: Marked "x-destructive":true and "x-beta":true, but the operation is tagged ["Transaction","transactions"] and requires scope transactions:write; its description says the call replaces the split and that an empty line_items array removes all splits.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the summary that this irreversibly replaces existing splits, and add a single canonical tag; confirm the required scope is transactions:write only.

findings.title: Vault creation requires two scopes but states no per-operation permission rules
findings.evidence: security: [{"oauth2":["cards:read_vault","limits:write"]}] — both scopes are listed in one security requirement object, and the summary is "Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details".
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether both scopes are required together (AND) or alternatively (OR), and describe what each grants in the operation description.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security requirement
findings.evidence: "security":[] while the operation creates financial reimbursements; every other reimbursement operation requires oauth2 reimbursements:read or reimbursements:write. The 401 response is documented, which implies auth is needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Set security to [{"oauth2":["reimbursements:write"]}] or explain why this endpoint is unauthenticated.

findings.title: Physical card POST lists no 401/403 and no scope note in description
findings.evidence: Responses include 200 and 400 with "description":"Error" and content of type "string", while other operations return DeveloperApiErrorResponse with error_v2 and x-trace-id.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the standard DeveloperApiErrorResponse schema for 400 and document 401/403/404 consistently.

findings.title: Error responses inconsistent; many operations lack documented error shapes
findings.evidence: These operations document only a 200 response (or 200 plus nothing), though the same family uses 400 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse, and a missing card or reimbursement has no 404 entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 400/401/404 responses using DeveloperApiErrorResponse to every operation so an agent can branch on error_code.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" on a get operation; the operation description says it fetches a single virtual card.
findings.suggested_fix: Change summary to "Fetch a virtual card"; a model choosing tools by summary may call a read as a delete.

findings.title: Physical card GET uses 201 instead of 200 for success
findings.evidence: responses: {"201":{... "description":"Success"}} — no 200 response is defined for this GET.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response code to 200.

findings.title: Pagination parameter semantics differ and start is an unspecified opaque cursor
findings.evidence: start: "The ID of the last entity of the previous page" (type string), while the response page.next is a full URL template "https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1/<resources>?<new_params>"; physical card list has no start/page_size at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Document start as an opaque cursor copied from page.next, and make pagination parameters consistent across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Physical card list cannot paginate, yet its response is paginated
findings.evidence: Parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only; the response schema is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with page.next.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters, or state that results are not paginated.

findings.title: Naming: userId and user_id mixed in query parameters
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use "name":"userId"; transactions and reimbursements use "user_id"; transactions also uses "orderByAmountAsc" next to "order_by_amount_desc".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId to user_id and orderByAmountAsc to order_by_amount_asc, with a deprecation note for the old names.

findings.title: Date parameter ambiguity: from_date vs from_transaction_date and undocumented 'Data.' text
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements (to_transaction_date, from_date, to_date); GET /developer/v1/transactions (include_merchant_data, include_merchant_data on GET transaction)
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date has description "Data."; from_transaction_date says "after this date" while from_date says "created after this date"; GET /transactions/{transaction_id} include_merchant_data description is "Data."
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "Data." with real descriptions and state exactly which timestamp each date filter compares against and whether bounds are inclusive.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload: reimbursement_id vs reimbursee_id unclear chaining
findings.evidence: Path is /reimbursement/submit-receipt (singular) while all other reimbursement paths are /reimbursements; reimbursee_id is required yet 'reimbursement_id' is optional and the body says 'If omitted, a new draft reimbursement will be created via OCR' with no stated relationship to reimbursee_id when attaching.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the path to match siblings and state whether reimbursee_id must match the existing reimbursement's owner when reimbursement_id is given.

findings.title: Upload receipt retry semantics conflict between header-less idempotency_key and none on others
findings.evidence: Upload uses a body field idempotency_key (required), while POST /cards/vault uses header X-Idempotency-Key (optional, minLength 1, maxLength 255); the vault POST creates spend limits and reveals PAN, yet the key is optional.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism across creating operations, make it required for vault creation and card creation, and document the replay behavior.

findings.title: Suspend and unsuspend use different methods for the same resource path with unclear responses
findings.evidence: POST summary "Suspend a card" description "The suspension is revertable."; DELETE summary "Unsuspend a card" with no description; DELETE on /cards/physical/{card_id} is "Terminate a card" with "irreversible".
findings.suggested_fix: Add descriptions to the DELETE suspension operation and note its effect on state, so the agent can distinguish reversible from irreversible deletes.

findings.title: No rate limit, retry, or backoff guidance anywhere in spec
findings.evidence: No description, x-rate-limit, or 429 response is defined on any operation; the only error responses are 400/401 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Document per-key rate limits, add 429 responses with Retry-After, and describe safe retry behavior for each error class.

findings.title: Page size limits stated inconsistently or missing
findings.evidence: Reimbursements and transactions say 'must be between 2 and 100'; virtual cards list has page_size with default 20 but no min/max; physical cards list has no pagination params at all despite returning PaginatedResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum/maximum to page_size schema on every paginated list and document the same bounds everywhere.

findings.title: Physical card list has no pagination parameters
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with page.next, but parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters with documented bounds, matching other list endpoints.

findings.title: Pagination styles and cursor semantics differ across lists
findings.evidence: Transactions and reimbursements use 'include_count' and total_count; virtual cards and physical cards do not. 'start' is documented as 'the ID of the last entity of the previous page' with type string and no guarantee of stability.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one pagination contract (cursor, page_size bounds, optional count) across all list operations and document cursor opacity and stability.

findings.title: Idempotency key inconsistent: optional on one endpoint, required in body on another
findings.evidence: Vault creation marks X-Idempotency-Key 'required: false'; receipt upload requires body field idempotency_key. Other POSTs (physical card create, mileage reimbursement, suspension) have no idempotency mechanism at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply one idempotency mechanism (header, required for all non-idempotent POSTs) with documented key lifetime and replay behavior.

findings.title: Vault card creation creates money-moving limits without idempotency requirement
findings.evidence: Header 'X-Idempotency-Key' is 'required: false' while the operation creates a spend limit and returns a card with PAN and CVV.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the idempotency key required and document duplicate-request behavior.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented for many operations
findings.evidence: Several operations list only success codes (e.g. PATCH only '200'); POST physical card returns 400 with a bare type string schema, not DeveloperApiErrorResponse; mileage POST lists only 401.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 400/401/403/404/409/429 consistently with DeveloperApiErrorResponse for every operation.

findings.title: Inconsistent success status codes for same resource
findings.evidence: get_physical_card_resource returns '201' as success; other fetches return 200. POST /cards/vault returns 201 while POST suspension returns 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for reads and document 201 only for resource creation; correct get_physical_card_resource.

findings.title: Misleading operation summaries and descriptions
findings.evidence: get_virtual_card_resource has summary 'Permanently delete this resource' while being a GET; get_physical_card_list_with_pagination operationIds and POST operationId 'post_physical_card_list_with_pagination' describe creation with pagination names.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and rename operationIds to match their actions.

findings.title: Vague or unexplained descriptions of parameters
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date description is just 'Data.'; include_merchant_data and trip_id say 'Data.' on transaction endpoints; the virtual card filter is named 'userId' while every other parameter uses snake_case 'user_id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write real descriptions for each parameter and rename userId to user_id (keeping the old name as a deprecated alias).

findings.title: Multiple ordering parameters conflict and naming is inconsistent
findings.evidence: Description says 'setting multiple ordering parameters is unsupported' but no mutual exclusion is expressed; 'orderByAmountAsc' is camelCase while others are snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a single sort parameter (e.g. sort=-user_transaction_time) with an enum, and document the default order.

findings.title: Split transaction PATCH is destructive but has no safety or retry guidance
findings.evidence: Marked 'x-destructive: true'; 'Send an empty line_items array to unsplit'; 'Omit to leave splits unchanged' with no documented retry or concurrent-update behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that replacing the split is idempotent for identical bodies, and describe concurrency handling and what clients should do after a timeout.

findings.title: Deprecated and duplicate fields with no removal timeline
findings.location: Transaction/SingleTransaction schemas: amount, currency_code, limit_id; ApiReimbursementAmount; spend_limit_id
findings.evidence: 'amount' is 'deprecated: true' yet typed as number in Transaction but string in SingleTransaction; 'limit_id' and 'spend_limit_id' are aliases of fund_id with no removal date.
findings.suggested_fix: Make types identical across schemas and publish a sunset policy for each deprecated field.

findings.title: Monetary amount representations are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is a decimal number; entity_amount.value is an integer in minor units; ApiReimbursementAmount.value is 'non-negative' while ApiSignedAmount allows negatives; CurrencyAmount.amount is an integer with no sign rule; split line items send 'amount' in minor units with no currency.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single money object (integer minor units plus currency and minor_unit_conversion_rate) everywhere and state sign rules once.

findings.title: Enum for reimbursement state and filters drift from schema
findings.evidence: Filter 'state' enum includes 'PENDING' while the description for the list filter says 'Filter by reimbursement state' with no statement of which value sets are stable; 'funding_source' enum is returned but not filterable.
findings.suggested_fix: Document enum stability policy and make filterable fields match returned fields.

findings.title: Mixed-case path and field naming across resources
findings.evidence: Path uses singular 'reimbursement' in submit-receipt but plural 'reimbursements' elsewhere; the 'userId' query param and camel-case operationIds conflict with snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Use plural resource names consistently in paths and snake_case for all parameters.

findings.title: GET /cards/physical/{card_id} lists 201 but no 404 or other errors
findings.evidence: Responses only define "201" (success) and "400" ("raises CardInvalidInput"). The success code is 201 rather than 200, and no 401/403/404 is documented.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success code to 200 and document 401, 403, and 404 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse.

findings.title: Many operations document no error responses at all
findings.location: PATCH /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}; DELETE /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id}/suspension; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual; GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual/{card_id}; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements; GET /developer/v1/reimbursements/{reimbursement_id}; PATCH /developer/v1/transactions/{transaction_id}; GET /developer/v1/cards/vault/{card_id}
findings.evidence: These operations define only success responses (e.g. PATCH card: "200" only; GET virtual card: "200" only; GET reimbursement: "200" only), while sibling operations such as GET /cards/physical/{card_id} document "400" with DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the same 400/401/404 error responses with DeveloperApiErrorResponse to every operation that accepts IDs or bodies.

findings.title: Error responses on POST /cards/physical use untyped string schema
findings.evidence: "400":{"description":"Error","content":{"application/json":{"schema":{"type":"string"}}}}
findings.suggested_fix: Use $ref DeveloperApiErrorResponse, as the other 400 responses do, so the client gets a typed error object.

findings.title: Error responses declared inconsistently across the API
findings.evidence: POST /reimbursements/mileage has only "200" and "401" (no 400 for invalid body). POST /reimbursement/submit-receipt documents 400/401/404 but no error case for the 201 path. POST /cards/vault only documents "400" with no 401 even though it requires security.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the same set of error codes (400, 401, 403, 404, 429 if used) on each write endpoint, and state which errors each one can return.

findings.title: Missing security on mileage creation endpoint
findings.evidence: "security":[]} while the operation returns "401" Unauthorized. Every other write operation declares oauth2 scopes (e.g. POST /reimbursement/submit-receipt uses "reimbursements:write").
findings.suggested_fix: Add security: [{oauth2: ["reimbursements:write"]}] and remove the empty override.

findings.title: Path naming inconsistent: reimbursement vs reimbursements
findings.evidence: Path "/developer/v1/reimbursement/submit-receipt" uses singular "reimbursement", while all other reimbursement paths use "/developer/v1/reimbursements" and "/developer/v1/reimbursements/mileage".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to /developer/v1/reimbursements/submit-receipt, keeping the old path documented as deprecated if needed.

findings.title: Inconsistent query param casing and paths for virtual cards
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/cards/virtual (query params userId, entity_id, is_terminated); GET /developer/v1/transactions (orderByAmountAsc, order_by_amount_desc)
findings.evidence: Query "userId" is camelCase while "user_id" is used elsewhere; "orderByAmountAsc" is camelCase while the sibling "order_by_amount_desc" is snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Use snake_case consistently: user_id and order_by_amount_asc. Keep the old names as deprecated aliases if they must stay.

findings.title: Pagination parameters differ between list endpoints
findings.evidence: Only the virtual-cards list defines "start" and "page_size" with a default of 20 and "page_size" is absent from physical cards. Physical cards returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with no start/page_size parameters at all. Transactions alone has include_count, which can return total_count.
findings.suggested_fix: Give all list endpoints the same pagination parameters (start, page_size with bounds) and document why total_count exists only on transactions.

findings.title: page_size bounds are not enforced in the schema
findings.evidence: Description says "The value must be between 2 and 100", but the schema is only {"default":20,"type":"integer"} with no minimum or maximum.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "minimum": 2 and "maximum": 100 to the schema so generated clients validate the range.

findings.title: Physical cards list uses non-standard response for 400 description
findings.evidence: Description of 400 is "raises CardInvalidInput" — an internal exception name rather than a documented error condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the actual invalid input conditions in plain language, e.g. which filter combinations are rejected.

findings.title: Nullable fields in Reimbursement list lack documented meaning
findings.evidence: Schema lists "employee_id" as "nullable":true with no description of when it is null; "distance" is nullable with the description 'for mileage reimbursements' but no statement that it is null for other types; "payee_amount" is nullable.
findings.suggested_fix: State the conditions under which each nullable field is null, and mark it as required or optional consistently.

findings.title: Deprecated amount field still typed as number, sibling typed as string
findings.evidence: In Transaction, "amount" is {"deprecated":true,"type":"number"}, but in SingleTransaction the same field is {"deprecated":true,"type":"string"}.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for the same field in both schemas, and align the deprecated field's documentation.

findings.title: Transaction.required omits many fields that are nullable or present
findings.evidence: Both schemas list "card_holder" absent from required, though card_holder is documented; "merchant_category_code" and "fund_id" are missing from required in both schemas while also readOnly. Fields like "amount" are not required but "entity_amount" is required and nullable.
findings.suggested_fix: Review the required arrays so non-null guarantees match the actual API behavior, and document the nullable-but-required pairs.

findings.title: Reimbursement required array includes nullable fields with no nullability note
findings.evidence: Required list includes "accounting_date", "approved_at", "distance", "employee_id" and others that are declared "nullable":true, while "created_at" and "id" are required and non-nullable.
findings.suggested_fix: Document clearly that these fields are always present but may be null, so generated types use optional-and-nullable rather than surprise nulls.

findings.title: Card vault endpoint returns PAN/CVV with no declared protection
findings.evidence: CardDetails.properties.pan 'Primary account number(PAN) of the card.' and cvv 'Card verfication value.' are plain strings; operation has only security oauth2 cards:read_vault and no x-headers, step-up, or response-caching constraints declared.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare Cache-Control: no-store on responses, mark pan/cvv as writeOnly/sensitive, and document an extra authorization requirement or restricted scope.

findings.title: Full card number exposed in physical card shipping schema
findings.evidence: "full_card_number":{"type":"string","description":"The full card number."} is returned under CardShipping, which is embedded in GET /developer/v1/cards/physical/{card_id} responses under cards:read scope.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove full_card_number from the general PhysicalCard read model or gate it behind cards:read_vault with no-store caching.

findings.title: PAN and CVV in PCICardDetails lack format or constraints
findings.evidence: pan {"type":"string"} and cvv {"type":"string"} have no pattern, minLength, maxLength, or writeOnly marker, while 'expiration' is described only as 'MMYY' text with no pattern.
findings.suggested_fix: Add pattern/length constraints (e.g., cvv ^[0-9]{3,4}$, expiration ^(0[1-9]|1[0-2])[0-9]{2}$) and mark sensitive fields clearly.

findings.title: POST /cards/physical and mileage POST lack declared security
findings.evidence: "security":[]` on the mileage create operation, while all other operations declare oauth2 scopes; responses list only a 401.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the oauth2 scope (e.g., reimbursements:write) for this operation or document why it is public.

findings.title: Pagination parameter naming inconsistent across list endpoints
findings.evidence: Virtual cards filter is 'userId' while physical cards and reimbursements use 'user_id'; transactions use 'order_by_date_asc' but virtual cards and transactions use 'orderByAmountAsc' vs 'order_by_amount_desc'.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize all query parameters on snake_case (userId→user_id, orderByAmountAsc→order_by_amount_asc).

findings.title: Same concept named differently: limit vs spend_limit vs fund
findings.evidence: The fund concept appears as limit_id, spend_limit_id, spend_allocation_id, and fund_id across endpoints, with 'limit_id' described as 'Alias of fund'.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one canonical name (fund_id) and mark the others deprecated consistently across all endpoints.

findings.title: Inconsistent pagination parameter and response shapes
findings.evidence: Virtual card list has 'start' and 'page_size' with default 20 but no maximum; transactions responses include total_count/total_count_capped via DeveloperAPICountedPage, while the virtual cards response uses DeveloperAPINestedPage with no count; 'page_size' is described as 'between 2 and 100' but has no minimum/maximum in schema.
findings.suggested_fix: Encode page_size minimum 2 and maximum 100 in schema for all list endpoints and use one page object across them.

findings.title: Physical card list 'id' fields lack pagination; start cursor undocumented
findings.evidence: Physical card list has no 'start' or 'page_size' parameters, yet returns PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with a page.next link.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters matching the other list endpoints, or remove the pagination envelope.

findings.title: Amount fields use mixed types and units
findings.location: Transaction.amount; ApiSignedAmount.value; CurrencyAmount.amount; ApiReimbursementAmount.value; GET /developer/v1/transactions min_amount/max_amount
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is {"type":"number"} (deprecated) while entity_amount.value is an integer minor unit; SingleTransaction.amount is {"type":"string"}; min_amount is oneOf decimal string or number with no unit stated.
findings.suggested_fix: Use integer minor units everywhere, remove the conflicting amount type, and state the unit in min_amount/max_amount descriptions.

findings.title: Date filter formats are inconsistent
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements (from_transaction_date, from_date, from_submitted_at); PATCH transaction, reimbursement.transaction_date
findings.evidence: Reimbursement list filters use format date-time, Reimbursement.transaction_date uses format date, and 'to_transaction_date' has description 'Data.' with no meaningful text.
findings.suggested_fix: Use consistent date/date-time formats per concept and replace placeholder descriptions like 'Data.' with real descriptions.

findings.title: Placeholder and missing descriptions on parameters
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date has description "Data."; include_merchant_data has description "Data." on the single-transaction endpoint.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace placeholder descriptions with accurate text describing the filter's semantics.

findings.title: Operation summaries contradict their actions
findings.evidence: GET virtual card has summary "Permanently delete this resource" while it is a read operation; DELETE physical card says 'Terminate a card'.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the GET summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and align terminology for physical card deletion.

findings.title: Inconsistent 2xx codes and error documentation across operations
findings.evidence: GET single physical card returns 201 instead of 200; POST /cards/physical 400 error uses schema type string while other 400s use DeveloperApiErrorResponse; PATCH has no 400/401/404 responses.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for GET, use DeveloperApiErrorResponse for all error responses, and document 401/404 consistently.

findings.title: Idempotency key defined inconsistently
findings.evidence: Vault creation takes optional header X-Idempotency-Key, while receipt upload requires body field idempotency_key; POST /cards/physical and POST /reimbursements/mileage have no idempotency mechanism.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism (header) across all POST endpoints and make it required for money-moving or card-creating operations.

findings.title: Transaction amount fields lack unit and sign clarity
findings.evidence: "amount":{"deprecated":true,"description":"Deprecated. Use `entity_amount`.","type":"number"} while SingleTransaction.amount is typed "type":"string". Same field, different types across schemas.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type for `amount` in both schemas, state its unit (major units or minor units), or remove it given the deprecation.

findings.title: Minor-unit amounts in split endpoint lack currency context
findings.evidence: "amount":{"description":"Amount in minor units (e.g. 5000 = $50.00).","type":"integer"} with no currency field or range, while ApiAccountingSplitLineItemRequestBody has no currency_code and the split must sum to the transaction amount in an unspecified currency.
findings.suggested_fix: Document the currency the split amounts are denominated in, whether it is the entity settlement currency, and whether negative values are allowed for refunds.

findings.title: Spend limit amount has no unit or currency requirement
findings.evidence: "amount":{"description":"the amount of money represented in the smallest denomination...","type":"integer"} with no minimum; "currency_code":{"default":"USD"}. No minimum or maximum, and the request schema lacks a `minimum` even though limits must be positive.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum (for example 1 or 0), maximum, and an explicit currency enum or supported-currency list for limit requests.

findings.title: Allowed overage percent has inconsistent type declarations
findings.evidence: Request: "maximum":100,"minimum":0,"oneOf":[{"format":"decimal","type":"string"},{"type":"number"}]; response: "format":"decimal","type":"string". Request accepts string or number; response only returns string; the `maximum`/`minimum` are placed outside oneOf.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one wire type (string decimal preferred for money-like values), state the precision, and apply the bounds consistently to both request and response.

findings.title: Timestamp formats are inconsistent and malformed in examples
findings.evidence: Example values such as "created_at":"2023-08-20T:00:00+00:00" and "submitted_at":"2023-08-20T:00:00+00:00" are not valid ISO8601 date-times; Transaction.accounting_date is format date-time but PhysicalCard.created_at is format date-time with example "2022-05-04T00:00:00+00:00".
findings.suggested_fix: Correct examples to full ISO8601 timestamps (for example 2023-08-20T00:00:00Z) and state the timezone rule.

findings.title: Transaction state enum mixes filter sentinel with real states
findings.evidence: Query enum: ["ALL","CLEARED","COMPLETION","DECLINED","ERROR","PENDING","PENDING_INITIATION"]; response state enum includes "ALL" too. A response record can never legitimately be ALL.
findings.suggested_fix: Separate the filter enum from the response enum and remove ALL from the response state enum.

findings.title: Date and datetime filters have no timezone or range rules
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements (from_transaction_date, to_transaction_date, from_date, to_date) and GET /developer/v1/transactions (from_date, to_date)
findings.evidence: "to_transaction_date" description is just "Data."; from_date is "format":"date-time" with no timezone or inclusive/exclusive statement, while from_transaction_date says "after this date" and from_date (transactions) says "after" vs "after this date" elsewhere.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe each boundary as inclusive or exclusive, require a timezone offset, and replace the placeholder 'Data.' description.

findings.title: Pagination page_size range is not enforced in schema
findings.evidence: Description: "The value must be between 2 and 100." but schema is only {"default":20,"type":"integer"} with no minimum or maximum.
findings.suggested_fix: Add "minimum":2 and "maximum":100 to the schema so clients and generators can validate it.

findings.title: Pagination cursor 'start' is an untyped opaque string with no contract
findings.evidence: "description":"The ID of the last entity of the previous page...","schema":{"type":"string"}. The physical cards list has no pagination params at all, and the `next` links use placeholder "<resources>?<new_params>".
findings.suggested_fix: Document start as an opaque cursor, prefer using the next URL, and add pagination parameters to the physical cards list or explain why it is unpaginated.

findings.title: Physical card list has no pagination controls
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with page.next, but parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only; no start or page_size.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters matching the other list endpoints, or document the maximum result size.

findings.title: Enum of reimbursement state is huge and can change without versioning
findings.evidence: Enum includes 25 values such as "EXPORT_MARKED_AS_FAILED", "REIMBURSED_VIA_PUSH" and "PUSH_PAYMENT_INITIATED", with no statement on whether new values may be added.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that enums are open and clients must handle unknown values, and publish a deprecation policy.

findings.title: Virtual card list filter uses inconsistent parameter naming
findings.evidence: Virtual cards: "name":"userId" while every other filter is snake_case (user_id, entity_id). Transactions: "name":"orderByAmountAsc" alongside order_by_amount_desc.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to user_id and order_by_amount_asc, keeping the old names as deprecated aliases.

findings.title: Reimbursement user_id query parameter is undocumented and duplicated
findings.evidence: The user_id parameter has no description, unlike all other parameters on the same operation, and there is no description of how it interacts with reimbursee-related filters.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a description stating what user_id filters (reimbursee or submitter).

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload has undefined file constraints
findings.evidence: "receipt":{... "UploadedFileRequestBody" format binary} with no maxLength, allowed MIME types, or size limit. The description only says 'Receipt image or PDF'.
findings.suggested_fix: Document accepted MIME types, maximum file size, and the expected behavior on oversize files.

findings.title: Idempotency key is inconsistent across endpoints
findings.evidence: Vault: header "X-Idempotency-Key" with minLength 1 and maxLength 255. Receipt upload: body field "idempotency_key" with no length limits and no statement of retention window or whether it is required (it is listed in required).
findings.suggested_fix: Use one mechanism (header with the same length bounds) across all POST endpoints and document the retention window and duplicate-key response.

findings.title: Reimbursement state values lack clear approval-state meanings
findings.evidence: State enum includes APPROVED, PENDING, INIT, DRAFT, REJECTED, PROCESSING, EXPORTED, REIMBURSED, REIMBURSED_VIA_PUSH, MANUALLY_REIMBURSED, etc. Descriptions are terse, e.g. "INIT":"Init", "PENDING":"Pending Review", "PUSH_PAYMENT_FAILED":"Payment failed", "EXPORT_FAILED":"Payment failed".
findings.suggested_fix: Define each state's meaning, which states mean money has moved, and which are terminal, and make the two 'Payment failed' labels distinct.

findings.title: Transaction state and approval_status lack defined meanings
findings.evidence: approval_status enum: AWAITING_EMPLOYEE, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_CHANGES_REQUESTED, AWAITING_EMPLOYEE_MISSING_ITEMS, AWAITING_REVIEWER, FULLY_APPROVED, but no x-enum-descriptions are given. The state enum has descriptions but 'COMPLETION' and 'ERROR' are vague.
findings.suggested_fix: Add x-enum-descriptions for approval_status and state the required action and who acts for each value.

findings.title: Reimbursement 'approved' filter and approved_at are unclear
findings.evidence: "Filter for reimbursements that are approved or not approved. If not specified, returns all reimbursements." and approved_at: "Time at which the reimbursement is approved." No field says who approved it.
findings.suggested_fix: State which approver is recorded and whether approved_at changes if a reimbursement is re-approved.

findings.title: No approver identity or approval history in any response
findings.evidence: Reimbursement has created_at, submitted_at, approved_at, updated_at, but no approved_by, rejected_by, or history field. Transaction has updated_at only, described as 'Approximate transaction updated timestamp'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add fields or an audit endpoint identifying who approved, rejected, or changed each item and when.

findings.title: updated_at is described as approximate and computed
findings.evidence: "Approximate transaction updated timestamp used by the `updated_after` filter. Computed as the latest of user transaction time, settlement time, and transaction interaction state update time."
findings.suggested_fix: Explain what changes count as an update and whether a memo or category change moves this timestamp, so audit windows are reliable.

findings.title: Amount fields use different units and types
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is a deprecated 'number' (e.g. 90.0, dollars) while entity_amount.value is an integer in cents (9000). SingleTransaction.amount is typed 'string'. Transaction.entity_amount is signed; ApiReimbursementAmount.value is 'non-negative'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one type and unit for all amounts and document the unit in each description, including whether the value is dollars or cents.

findings.title: Amount sign convention is inconsistent across schemas
findings.evidence: ApiSignedAmount: "May be negative for refunds or credits." ApiReimbursementAmount: "The non-negative amount" with minimum 0. Reimbursement paybacks (PAYBACK_FULL, PAYBACK_PARTIAL) have no stated sign.
findings.suggested_fix: State whether reimbursement payback amounts are positive or negative and which direction money flows.

findings.title: Date fields lack timezone and meaning clarity
findings.evidence: transaction_date is type 'date' while created_at is 'date-time'. Filter descriptions: from_transaction_date 'Filter by underlying transaction date (after this date).' and to_transaction_date 'Data.' ; from_date 'created after this date' vs Transaction from_date 'user_transaction_time'.
findings.suggested_fix: Make to_transaction_date's description meaningful, state inclusive/exclusive bounds, and name the exact timestamp each date filter uses.

findings.title: Transaction filter from_date uses a different date than list labels imply
findings.evidence: "Filter for transactions with a `user_transaction_time` after the given date" while order_by_date_asc says "Sort transactions by `user_transaction_date`" (a different field name).
findings.suggested_fix: Use one consistent date field name and state whether from_date and order_by_date refer to the same timestamp.

findings.title: Accounting date meaning depends on undisclosed settings
findings.evidence: "Based on the cleared date, transaction date, or a manually overridden date, depending on your accounting preferences in Ramp." and reimbursement: "uses the transaction date or reviewed date according to accounting sync settings".
findings.suggested_fix: Add a field showing which source produced the value (cleared, transaction, reviewed, or override) so the compliance reviewer can see it.

findings.title: Split line item rules conflict or are undocumented
findings.evidence: Description: "Send line_items with amounts (in minor units)" but ApiTransactionLineItem.amount is a CurrencyAmount object. Field selection says 'Provide exactly one of field_id or field_external_id' but neither is required in the schema. Operation is marked "x-destructive":true with no description of what is lost.
findings.suggested_fix: State the request amount format, enforce the 'exactly one' rules in the schema, and describe what existing memos or coding are overwritten.

findings.title: Mileage create endpoint has no auth and an unclear default
findings.evidence: "security":[] and the only response listed is 401 'Unauthorized'. Request field distance_units has no default or description and spend_allocation_id is described as 'the fund'.
findings.suggested_fix: Declare the required OAuth scope, and document the default distance unit and whether the fund is the same as the spend limit.

findings.title: Receipt upload retry behaviour and idempotency key duplicated
findings.evidence: Receipt upload takes idempotency_key in the form body and it is required, while the vault create uses header X-Idempotency-Key which is optional. Receipt schema description says only "Caller-supplied key that makes upload retries idempotent."
findings.suggested_fix: Use one mechanism for idempotency and state what happens when a key is reused with different content.

findings.title: Physical card 'state' and 'is_suspended' overlap without explanation
findings.evidence: state enum includes SUSPENDED, and is_suspended: 'Whether the card is suspended.' Suspend endpoint says "The suspension is revertable." but terminate says "irreversible" without saying who can reverse it.
findings.suggested_fix: Explain how the two fields relate and record who suspended the card and when.

findings.title: Transaction split PATCH is destructive yet mislabeled and undocumented for auth
findings.evidence: Marked "x-destructive":true and "x-beta":true, but the operation is tagged ["Transaction","transactions"] and requires scope transactions:write; its description says the call replaces the split and that an empty line_items array removes all splits.
findings.suggested_fix: State in the summary that this irreversibly replaces existing splits, and add a single canonical tag; confirm the required scope is transactions:write only.

findings.title: Vault creation requires two scopes but states no per-operation permission rules
findings.evidence: security: [{"oauth2":["cards:read_vault","limits:write"]}] — both scopes are listed in one security requirement object, and the summary is "Create a spend limit and retrieve sensitive card details".
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether both scopes are required together (AND) or alternatively (OR), and describe what each grants in the operation description.

findings.title: Mileage reimbursement POST declares no security requirement
findings.evidence: "security":[] while the operation creates financial reimbursements; every other reimbursement operation requires oauth2 reimbursements:read or reimbursements:write. The 401 response is documented, which implies auth is needed.
findings.suggested_fix: Set security to [{"oauth2":["reimbursements:write"]}] or explain why this endpoint is unauthenticated.

findings.title: Physical card POST lists no 401/403 and no scope note in description
findings.evidence: Responses include 200 and 400 with "description":"Error" and content of type "string", while other operations return DeveloperApiErrorResponse with error_v2 and x-trace-id.
findings.suggested_fix: Return the standard DeveloperApiErrorResponse schema for 400 and document 401/403/404 consistently.

findings.title: Error responses inconsistent; many operations lack documented error shapes
findings.evidence: These operations document only a 200 response (or 200 plus nothing), though the same family uses 400 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse, and a missing card or reimbursement has no 404 entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 400/401/404 responses using DeveloperApiErrorResponse to every operation so an agent can branch on error_code.

findings.title: Virtual card GET summary says 'Permanently delete this resource'
findings.evidence: "summary":"Permanently delete this resource" on a get operation; the operation description says it fetches a single virtual card.
findings.suggested_fix: Change summary to "Fetch a virtual card"; a model choosing tools by summary may call a read as a delete.

findings.title: Physical card GET uses 201 instead of 200 for success
findings.evidence: responses: {"201":{... "description":"Success"}} — no 200 response is defined for this GET.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the success response code to 200.

findings.title: Pagination parameter semantics differ and start is an unspecified opaque cursor
findings.evidence: start: "The ID of the last entity of the previous page" (type string), while the response page.next is a full URL template "https://api.ramp.com/developer/v1/<resources>?<new_params>"; physical card list has no start/page_size at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Document start as an opaque cursor copied from page.next, and make pagination parameters consistent across all list endpoints.

findings.title: Physical card list cannot paginate, yet its response is paginated
findings.evidence: Parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only; the response schema is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with page.next.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters, or state that results are not paginated.

findings.title: Naming: userId and user_id mixed in query parameters
findings.evidence: Virtual cards use "name":"userId"; transactions and reimbursements use "user_id"; transactions also uses "orderByAmountAsc" next to "order_by_amount_desc".
findings.suggested_fix: Rename userId to user_id and orderByAmountAsc to order_by_amount_asc, with a deprecation note for the old names.

findings.title: Date parameter ambiguity: from_date vs from_transaction_date and undocumented 'Data.' text
findings.location: GET /developer/v1/reimbursements (to_transaction_date, from_date, to_date); GET /developer/v1/transactions (include_merchant_data, include_merchant_data on GET transaction)
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date has description "Data."; from_transaction_date says "after this date" while from_date says "created after this date"; GET /transactions/{transaction_id} include_merchant_data description is "Data."
findings.suggested_fix: Replace "Data." with real descriptions and state exactly which timestamp each date filter compares against and whether bounds are inclusive.

findings.title: Reimbursement receipt upload: reimbursement_id vs reimbursee_id unclear chaining
findings.evidence: Path is /reimbursement/submit-receipt (singular) while all other reimbursement paths are /reimbursements; reimbursee_id is required yet 'reimbursement_id' is optional and the body says 'If omitted, a new draft reimbursement will be created via OCR' with no stated relationship to reimbursee_id when attaching.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the path to match siblings and state whether reimbursee_id must match the existing reimbursement's owner when reimbursement_id is given.

findings.title: Upload receipt retry semantics conflict between header-less idempotency_key and none on others
findings.evidence: Upload uses a body field idempotency_key (required), while POST /cards/vault uses header X-Idempotency-Key (optional, minLength 1, maxLength 255); the vault POST creates spend limits and reveals PAN, yet the key is optional.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one idempotency mechanism across creating operations, make it required for vault creation and card creation, and document the replay behavior.

findings.title: Suspend and unsuspend use different methods for the same resource path with unclear responses
findings.evidence: POST summary "Suspend a card" description "The suspension is revertable."; DELETE summary "Unsuspend a card" with no description; DELETE on /cards/physical/{card_id} is "Terminate a card" with "irreversible".
findings.suggested_fix: Add descriptions to the DELETE suspension operation and note its effect on state, so the agent can distinguish reversible from irreversible deletes.

findings.title: No rate limit, retry, or backoff guidance anywhere in spec
findings.evidence: No description, x-rate-limit, or 429 response is defined on any operation; the only error responses are 400/401 with DeveloperApiErrorResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Document per-key rate limits, add 429 responses with Retry-After, and describe safe retry behavior for each error class.

findings.title: Page size limits stated inconsistently or missing
findings.evidence: Reimbursements and transactions say 'must be between 2 and 100'; virtual cards list has page_size with default 20 but no min/max; physical cards list has no pagination params at all despite returning PaginatedResponse.
findings.suggested_fix: Add minimum/maximum to page_size schema on every paginated list and document the same bounds everywhere.

findings.title: Physical card list has no pagination parameters
findings.evidence: Response is PaginatedResponseApiPhysicalCardResource with page.next, but parameters are only user_id, display_name, include_activated_only, include_terminated_only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add start and page_size parameters with documented bounds, matching other list endpoints.

findings.title: Pagination styles and cursor semantics differ across lists
findings.evidence: Transactions and reimbursements use 'include_count' and total_count; virtual cards and physical cards do not. 'start' is documented as 'the ID of the last entity of the previous page' with type string and no guarantee of stability.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one pagination contract (cursor, page_size bounds, optional count) across all list operations and document cursor opacity and stability.

findings.title: Idempotency key inconsistent: optional on one endpoint, required in body on another
findings.evidence: Vault creation marks X-Idempotency-Key 'required: false'; receipt upload requires body field idempotency_key. Other POSTs (physical card create, mileage reimbursement, suspension) have no idempotency mechanism at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply one idempotency mechanism (header, required for all non-idempotent POSTs) with documented key lifetime and replay behavior.

findings.title: Vault card creation creates money-moving limits without idempotency requirement
findings.evidence: Header 'X-Idempotency-Key' is 'required: false' while the operation creates a spend limit and returns a card with PAN and CVV.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the idempotency key required and document duplicate-request behavior.

findings.title: Error responses undocumented for many operations
findings.evidence: Several operations list only success codes (e.g. PATCH only '200'); POST physical card returns 400 with a bare type string schema, not DeveloperApiErrorResponse; mileage POST lists only 401.
findings.suggested_fix: Document 400/401/403/404/409/429 consistently with DeveloperApiErrorResponse for every operation.

findings.title: Inconsistent success status codes for same resource
findings.evidence: get_physical_card_resource returns '201' as success; other fetches return 200. POST /cards/vault returns 201 while POST suspension returns 200.
findings.suggested_fix: Return 200 for reads and document 201 only for resource creation; correct get_physical_card_resource.

findings.title: Misleading operation summaries and descriptions
findings.evidence: get_virtual_card_resource has summary 'Permanently delete this resource' while being a GET; get_physical_card_list_with_pagination operationIds and POST operationId 'post_physical_card_list_with_pagination' describe creation with pagination names.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the summary to 'Fetch a virtual card' and rename operationIds to match their actions.

findings.title: Vague or unexplained descriptions of parameters
findings.evidence: to_transaction_date description is just 'Data.'; include_merchant_data and trip_id say 'Data.' on transaction endpoints; the virtual card filter is named 'userId' while every other parameter uses snake_case 'user_id'.
findings.suggested_fix: Write real descriptions for each parameter and rename userId to user_id (keeping the old name as a deprecated alias).

findings.title: Multiple ordering parameters conflict and naming is inconsistent
findings.evidence: Description says 'setting multiple ordering parameters is unsupported' but no mutual exclusion is expressed; 'orderByAmountAsc' is camelCase while others are snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a single sort parameter (e.g. sort=-user_transaction_time) with an enum, and document the default order.

findings.title: Split transaction PATCH is destructive but has no safety or retry guidance
findings.evidence: Marked 'x-destructive: true'; 'Send an empty line_items array to unsplit'; 'Omit to leave splits unchanged' with no documented retry or concurrent-update behavior.
findings.suggested_fix: Document that replacing the split is idempotent for identical bodies, and describe concurrency handling and what clients should do after a timeout.

findings.title: Deprecated and duplicate fields with no removal timeline
findings.location: Transaction/SingleTransaction schemas: amount, currency_code, limit_id; ApiReimbursementAmount; spend_limit_id
findings.evidence: 'amount' is 'deprecated: true' yet typed as number in Transaction but string in SingleTransaction; 'limit_id' and 'spend_limit_id' are aliases of fund_id with no removal date.
findings.suggested_fix: Make types identical across schemas and publish a sunset policy for each deprecated field.

findings.title: Monetary amount representations are inconsistent
findings.evidence: Transaction.amount is a decimal number; entity_amount.value is an integer in minor units; ApiReimbursementAmount.value is 'non-negative' while ApiSignedAmount allows negatives; CurrencyAmount.amount is an integer with no sign rule; split line items send 'amount' in minor units with no currency.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a single money object (integer minor units plus currency and minor_unit_conversion_rate) everywhere and state sign rules once.

findings.title: Enum for reimbursement state and filters drift from schema
findings.evidence: Filter 'state' enum includes 'PENDING' while the description for the list filter says 'Filter by reimbursement state' with no statement of which value sets are stable; 'funding_source' enum is returned but not filterable.
findings.suggested_fix: Document enum stability policy and make filterable fields match returned fields.

findings.title: Mixed-case path and field naming across resources
findings.evidence: Path uses singular 'reimbursement' in submit-receipt but plural 'reimbursements' elsewhere; the 'userId' query param and camel-case operationIds conflict with snake_case.
findings.suggested_fix: Use plural resource names consistently in paths and snake_case for all parameters.
